intro.title: What should your new app do?
intro.lead: Describe it and add any documents. Platon reads everything, asks a few questions, then sets the project up.
intro.placeholder: e.g. An app for field technicians to manage work orders. Dispatchers assign jobs, customers track their own.
intro.dropHint: or drop DOCX, PDF, XLSX, images

field.label: Field service
field.text: An app for our field technicians to manage work orders — today’s jobs, hours, parts and photos. Dispatchers assign jobs, customers track their own. Must work on phones with bad signal and send SMS.

purchase.label: Purchase approvals
purchase.text: Employees request purchases, managers approve within budget, finance pays.

onboarding.label: Client onboarding
onboarding.text: A portal where new clients upload documents and track onboarding steps.

inspections.label: Inspections
inspections.text: Inspectors run safety checklists on tablets and flag issues for follow-up.

feed.questionsIntro: Great. {n} quick questions — most are pre-filled, so you can mostly press Next.

signin.label: Sign-in
signin.hint: Pick any. Each method becomes a login option on the sign-in page.

modules.label: Modules
modules.text: Which modules should Platon turn on?
modules.hint: Pre-selected from your requirements. You can enable or remove modules later in Project settings.

theme.label: Look
theme.hint: The preview on the right updates as you choose.

langs.label: Languages
langs.text: Which languages do your users need?
langs.hint: The first one you pick is the default. Platon drafts translations for the rest.

team.label: Team
team.text: Who should build this with you?
team.hint: Search everyone in {org}. Roles work like GitLab: Owner, Maintainer, Developer, Reporter, Planner, Guest.

data.label: Data
data.hint: Jobs, parts and time entries are relational, so PostgreSQL fits best.
